```sql
WITH g AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           ol.order_id,
           pv.id                     AS variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)          AS q,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents)  AS r,
           GROUPING(ol.order_id)     AS is_variant_row
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN orders o            ON o.id = ol.order_id
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = ol.variant_id::uuid
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((pv.product_id, ol.order_id),
                             (pv.product_id, pv.id))
), agg AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_variant_row = 0)         AS order_count,
           (sum(q) FILTER (WHERE is_variant_row = 0))::bigint AS quantity,
           sum(r) FILTER (WHERE is_variant_row = 0)           AS revenue_cents,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_variant_row = 1)         AS variant_count
      FROM g
     GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       a.order_count,
       a.quantity,
       a.revenue_cents,
       a.variant_count
  FROM agg a
  JOIN products p ON p.id = a.product_id
 ORDER BY a.quantity DESC, a.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De twee `count(DISTINCT ...)` dwongen een sortering op (p.id, o.id) af die naar schijf liep. Ik vervang ze door één gehashte GROUPING SETS-aggregatie per (product, order) en per (product, variant). Daarna tel en sommeer ik per product, waarbij `quantity` naar bigint wordt gecast zodat het type gelijk blijft. Pas daarna worden de ~1750 resultaatrijen aan `products` gekoppeld, in plaats van alle ~81k regels met de brede productkolommen mee te sorteren.
